sources.used_for: Rounded “Say” dimensions: 7.4 ft span, 3.7 ft wrist span, 4 in shoulder span, 8 in maximum body width and 55 in overall length; paragraph total wing area 6.61 ft²; swan outline and approximately parallel-chord inner/tapered outer planform.
Qualitative separation into inner arm and outer hand wing panels, plus the proposal for a conventional tail, fin and rudder.

assumptions: Conversions use exactly 1 ft = 0.3048 m and 1 in = 0.0254 m.
Aspect ratio is derived as span²/area (8.284416767...), consistent with the page's rounded 8.29.
Each wing runs from half the 4 in shoulder span to half the 7.4 ft span, with its wrist at half the 3.7 ft wrist span.
The visual animation uses an assumed symmetric 14 degree inner-panel stroke and an additional 24 degree outer-panel articulation; these are presentation assumptions, not measured performance inputs.
Mass, atmosphere, force polar, 400 W drive, 65% propulsive factor, controls and contact rules are new benchmark assumptions supplied by this task and are not attributed to Stanley J. O. Tinn.
excluded_fields: The page 02 “3.135 ft” wing length; individual wing length is instead inferred from span and shoulder span.
The missing-table 7.83 comparison and the crossed-out 14% area argument on page 02.
Page 14 biological stroke-angle reference frames, elastic stiffness, vortex-lift landing hypothesis and unspecified curved-plate polar.
Any missing appendices, Standard Model Swan values, or prior human-carrying simulator values.
limitations: The photographs are historical notes, not a complete or validated ornithopter blueprint.
This is a point-mass, cycle-averaged educational model; wing panels are animated independently but do not produce resolved unsteady aerodynamic loads.
It is not a structural, aeroelastic, biological-flight or experimentally validated performance solver.
The fin, body sections, panel airfoils, colors and detailed tail geometry are visual interpretations because the sources do not fully specify them.
Publishing claims of physical validity would require evidence beyond this demonstration.
